title: Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines v. Agito
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the criteria for determining employer-employee relationships, applying the four-fold test. Workers who perform activities necessary and desirable to the usual business of the employer are considered regular employees regardless of the nomenclature of their contracts.
doctrine: The four-fold test determines the existence of an employer-employee relationship: (1) selection and engagement; (2) payment of wages; (3) power of dismissal; and (4) power of control. An employee who performs work necessary and desirable to the business is a regular employee under Article 280 of the Labor Code.
fullText:
BRION, J.:

The pivotal issue is whether the complainants are employees of Coca-Cola and, if so, whether they were illegally dismissed.

The existence of an employer-employee relationship is determined by the four-fold test: (1) the selection and engagement of the employee; (2) the payment of wages; (3) the power of dismissal; and (4) the employer's power to control the employee's conduct. The most important element is the employer's control of the employee's conduct.

Article 280 of the Labor Code provides that an employee who has been performing activities usually necessary or desirable in the usual business or trade of the employer shall be considered a regular employee. The law overrides stipulations in contracts that characterize regular employees as project or seasonal workers.
